findings.title: Stored XSS: note body rendered unescaped on /notes/:id

cvss.justification: POST /notes (src/server.ts:98-103) never calls currentUser, so an anonymous remote attacker can plant an arbitrary script that GET /notes/:id later interpolates unescaped at line 93 (`${row.body}`) into the HTML shown to any visitor — the route performs no owner check. Planting the payload requires no privileges or special conditions, but a victim must open the note URL for the script to execute. The flaw sits in server-side rendering while the impact lands in the victim's browser session (a different security authority), where the payload steals the non-HttpOnly `user` cookie and acts as the victim, so Scope is Changed. Confirmed impact is limited to the victim's session and data (C:L/I:L) with no availability effect.

findings.summary: The note body accepted by POST /notes is stored verbatim and later interpolated raw into the HTML of GET /notes/:id, so anyone can plant a script that runs in every visitor's browser.
findings.details:
`POST /notes` (src/server.ts lines 98-103) writes `String(req.body.body ?? "")` straight into the notes table with no filtering, and the handler never calls `currentUser`, so no authentication is required to create a note.

`GET /notes/:id` (src/server.ts lines 80-96) reads the row back and at line 93 interpolates the stored value directly into the document:

```ts
`<section class="card">${row.body}</section>${back}`
```

That string becomes the `body` argument of `page()` (src/views.ts lines 37-39), which places it inside `<main>${body}</main>` of a full HTML document, and `res.send()` delivers it as `text/html; charset=utf-8`.

There is no encoding anywhere on this path. A repo-wide search for `escape`, `sanitize`, `DOMPurify`, or `innerHTML` finds nothing except the `encodeURIComponent` at src/server.ts line 73, which encodes a Set-Cookie header value, not HTML output.

The route also performs no owner check (the comment on line 83 acknowledges the IDOR), so the payload is not even limited to the note creator: any user who opens the note id executes it.
findings.poc:
Create the stored payload, which needs no authentication because `POST /notes` never checks the current user.

```http
POST /notes HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

body=%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.cookie)%3C%2Fscript%3E
```

Open the note that was just created, id 3, since notes 1 and 2 are seeded.

```http
GET /notes/3 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
```

The HTML response contains `<section class="card"><script>alert(document.cookie)</script></section>` and the browser executes the script.
findings.impact: Any visitor who opens the note URL, signed in or not, gets attacker-chosen JavaScript executed in the application origin. The payload can read the `user` cookie that serves as identity, act as the victim, and deface the page. Because note creation is unauthenticated and note viewing has no owner check, an anonymous attacker can plant the payload and target every user of the app.

validation.reasoning: POST /notes stores String(req.body.body) verbatim with no auth check, and GET /notes/:id interpolates row.body raw into `<section class="card">${row.body}</section>` which page() (src/views.ts) embeds unescaped in the HTML document served as text/html; a repo-wide grep finds no escape/sanitize anywhere and no CSP middleware, so the url-encoded <script> payload in the PoC is stored and executed on GET /notes/3 (notes 1-2 are seeded in db.ts).
validation.confirmedImpact: Any anonymous attacker can plant arbitrary JavaScript via unauthenticated POST /notes, and every visitor who opens the note URL (no owner check) executes it in the app origin, allowing theft of the non-HttpOnly `user` session cookie and actions as the victim.

findings.suggestedFix:
The root cause is that the stored `notes.body` value is interpolated raw into the HTML document on `GET /notes/:id`, with no output encoding anywhere on the path. The fix is to HTML-escape the value at the point where it enters the template, so any note content is rendered as text and can never be parsed as markup.

**Location:** `src/server.ts`, line 5 and line 93

```diff
--- a/src/server.ts
+++ b/src/server.ts
@@ -5,1 +5,1 @@ line 5
-import { card, loginCard, noteList, page, searchCard } from "./views";
+import { card, escapeHtml, loginCard, noteList, page, searchCard } from "./views";
@@ -93,1 +93,1 @@ line 93
-        `<section class="card">${row.body}</section>${back}`, // stored XSS on display
+        `<section class="card">${escapeHtml(row.body)}</section>${back}`,
```

**Location:** `src/views.ts`, before line 37

```diff
--- a/src/views.ts
+++ b/src/views.ts
@@ -37,1 +37,9 @@ before line 37
+export const escapeHtml = (value: string) =>
+  value
+    .replace(/&/g, "&")
+    .replace(/</g, "<")
+    .replace(/>/g, ">")
+    .replace(/"/g, """)
+    .replace(/'/g, "'");
+
 export const page = (title: string, purpose: string, body: string, user?: string) =>
```

- `GET /search` interpolates `q` into the results card heading unescaped; wrap it in `escapeHtml` as well.
- The `Note ${req.params.id}` title on `GET /notes/:id` reaches `<title>`/`<h1>` unescaped; escape it the same way.

findings.title: Reflected XSS: search term rendered unescaped in /search results heading

cvss.justification: The `q` query parameter is interpolated raw into the card heading at src/server.ts line 58 and `card()`/`page()` in src/views.ts perform no HTML escaping, so a crafted GET /search?q=... URL executes attacker JavaScript in the app's origin; the route renders the heading regardless of the `user` cookie, so no authentication is needed (PR:N), but the victim must follow the attacker's link (UI:R) over the network (AV:N, AC:L). Scope is Unchanged since execution stays within the same Express app origin with no other component to cross into. Confirmed impact is arbitrary JS in the browser — cookie theft of the plaintext `user` cookie, actions as the victim, and phishing — but the app's data is a small in-memory note store (readable via the separate IDOR anyway) and no availability impact was validated, so C:L/I:L/A:N is the realistic scoring rather than all-High.

findings.summary: The `q` query parameter is interpolated raw into the results card heading of the /search page, so a crafted link runs script in the victim's browser.
findings.details:
`GET /search` reads the query string at src/server.ts line 42 (`const q = String(req.query.q ?? "")`) and at line 58 interpolates it into a card heading: ```ts searchCard(user) + card(`Results for ${q}`, "Open a note to read it.", results) ``` `card()` (src/views.ts lines 41-42) embeds the heading with no escaping, producing `

${heading}

${hint}

${body}
`, and `page()` (src/views.ts lines 37-39) wraps it into the HTML document that `res.send()` returns as `text/html`. The heading is rendered whether or not the visitor is signed in, because only the `results` block depends on the `user` cookie, so the injection needs no authentication. Note that the same `q` value is passed to SQLite as a bound parameter in the LIKE clause (src/server.ts lines 46-49), so the database call is safe; only the HTML output is vulnerable.
findings.poc:
Send a search request with an encoded script tag in the `q` parameter, no cookie required. ```http GET /search?q=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E HTTP/1.1 Host: localhost:3000 ``` The response contains `

Results for

` in a `text/html` page, so the script runs, and the same URL can be sent to a victim as a link.
findings.impact: Any user who follows an attacker-crafted search link gets script execution in the application origin. The attacker can read the identity cookie, perform actions as the victim, and phish page content, and no authentication is required to reach the vulnerable page.

validation.reasoning:
src/server.ts:42 reads req.query.q unvalidated and line 58 interpolates it into card(`Results for ${q}`, ...); card() in src/views.ts embeds the heading as raw

${heading}

with no escaping, and res.send() serves it as text/html. No auth is needed since the heading renders regardless of the user cookie, and no escaping exists anywhere on the path (grep confirms only encodeURIComponent on the login cookie). The PoC works as written: Express decodes q=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E into a live
validation.confirmedImpact: Any user who follows an attacker-crafted /search?q=... link gets arbitrary JavaScript execution in the application origin, enabling cookie theft, actions as the victim, and content phishing, with no authentication required.

findings.suggestedFix:
The root cause is that the raw `q` query string is interpolated straight into the HTML heading with no escaping, so any markup in it executes; the fix adds an `escapeHtml` helper in `src/views.ts` and runs `q` through it at the one place it reaches HTML, while the untouched raw value keeps feeding the bound LIKE parameter so search behavior is unchanged.

**Location:** `src/server.ts`, line 5 and line 58

```diff
--- a/src/server.ts
+++ b/src/server.ts
@@ -5,1 +5,1 @@ line 5
-import { card, loginCard, noteList, page, searchCard } from "./views";
+import { card, escapeHtml, loginCard, noteList, page, searchCard } from "./views";
@@ -58,1 +58,1 @@ line 58
-        searchCard(user) + card(`Results for ${q}`, "Open a note to read it.", results), // reflected XSS
+        searchCard(user) + card(`Results for ${escapeHtml(q)}`, "Open a note to read it.", results),
```

**Location:** `src/views.ts`, after line 30

```diff
--- a/src/views.ts
+++ b/src/views.ts
@@ -30,1 +30,9 @@ after line 30
 </style>`;
+
+export const escapeHtml = (value: string) =>
+  value
+    .replace(/&/g, "&")
+    .replace(/</g, "<")
+    .replace(/>/g, ">")
+    .replace(/"/g, """)
+    .replace(/'/g, "'");
```

Further steps:

- `src/views.ts` `bar()` and the home card hint (`The notes that ${user} owns.`) interpolate the `user` cookie value unescaped — route those through `escapeHtml` as well.
- `req.params.id` is interpolated unescaped into the `/notes/:id` page title in `src/server.ts` — escape it the same way.
- `row.body` is rendered raw in `/notes/:id` (stored XSS) — escape it at render unless notes are intentionally allowed to carry markup.
